mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW Z4 20i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW Z4 20i engine replacement typically costs £1,300-£3,600 supply-only for rebuilt N46 or N20 units, or £2,500-£5,500 fitted by a specialist. Used N46B20 engines: £800-£1,600 depending on mileage and condition. Used N20B20A engines: £1,000-£2,200. Reconditioned N46/N20 units: £1,300-£2,800 with 12-month warranty. Rebuilt N46/N20 engines: £1,800-£3,600 with upgraded components. Professional fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on workshop rates.

mainEntity.name: Does the BMW Z4 sDrive20i N20 engine have timing chain problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the N20B20A engine in the E89 Z4 sDrive20i is known for timing chain guide failure. The plastic guides can break, causing chain slack and catastrophic engine damage. This is particularly prevalent on engines produced before 2015. Symptoms include a rattling noise on cold start and a 'tractor-like' sound from the engine. If you hear these sounds, do not drive the car - have it inspected immediately. Preventative chain replacement is far cheaper than a full engine replacement.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW Z4 E85 2.0i N46 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N46B20 is generally reliable when properly maintained, but it has age-related issues. The most common problems are oil leaks from the valve cover gasket and oil filter housing, timing chain tensioner wear, and cooling system failures. Regular oil changes using the correct specification oil and prompt attention to leaks are essential to N46 longevity. The N46 is not as problematic as the N20's timing chain issue, but it requires proactive maintenance.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of N20 timing chain failure on a BMW Z4 sDrive20i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs are a rattling noise on cold start that may diminish as the engine warms, a 'tractor-like' sound from the engine, and in advanced cases, the engine management light illuminating with camshaft correlation codes. If you notice any of these symptoms on your Z4 sDrive20i, do not drive the car - have the timing chain inspected immediately. Ignoring the rattle can lead to complete engine destruction.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a high-mileage BMW Z4 20i?

acceptedAnswer.text: For an E89 Z4 sDrive20i worth £6,000-£14,000, a £2,200-£3,600 rebuilt N20B20A engine can make financial sense if the body, gearbox and interior are sound. For an E85 Z4 2.0i worth £3,000-£6,000, carefully evaluate whether a rebuilt engine is financially sensible - for a car in excellent condition, the investment can be justified. A rebuilt engine with warranty offers peace of mind that a high-mileage used unit cannot match.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the BMW Z4 20i E85 and E89 engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The E85 Z4 20i (2005-2008) uses the N46B20 naturally aspirated 2.0-litre four-cylinder producing 150hp. The E89 Z4 sDrive20i (2011-2016) uses the N20B20A turbocharged 2.0-litre four-cylinder producing 184hp. They are completely different engine families - the N20 is turbocharged with direct injection, while the N46 is naturally aspirated with port injection. When ordering a replacement engine, ensure you match the correct engine code to your Z4 20i's generation.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW Z4 20i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW Z4 20i spans two distinct generations with two very different four-cylinder engines. The E85 Z4 20i (2005-2008) used the naturally aspirated N46B20 inline-four, while the E89 Z4 sDrive20i (2011-2016) introduced the turbocharged N20B20A with BMW TwinPower Turbo technology. The 20i badge represented the entry point to Z4 ownership across both generations, offering accessible performance with four-cylinder efficiency.

milestones.description: March 2005 - E85 Z4 20i introduced with N46B20 2.0L naturally aspirated four-cylinder, 150hp (110kW)
2008 - N46B20 remains the sole engine for the E85 Z4 20i throughout production
September 2011 - E89 Z4 sDrive20i launched with N20B20A 2.0L TwinPower Turbo four-cylinder, 184hp (135kW)
2016 - N20B20A powers the E89 Z4 sDrive20i with 270Nm torque from 1,250rpm
E89 Z4 production ends; the 20i badge retired until the G29 generation

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW Z4 20i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - from the E85 N46 to the E89 N20 turbo.

commonProblems.h2: BMW Z4 20i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW Z4 20i is powered by two very different four-cylinder engines depending on the generation. The N46 (E85, 2005-2008) is a naturally aspirated unit with age-related oil leak and timing chain concerns, while the N20 (E89, 2011-2016) is a turbocharged engine with a well-documented timing chain guide failure. Below we break down the most common failures on both Z4 20i engines, what you'll pay at a dealer versus a specialist, and when replacement is the only sensible answer. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: N20 Timing Chain Guide Failure - Why BMW Z4 sDrive20i Engines Fail Catastrophically
problems.rootCause: The N20 timing chain guides are made of plastic that becomes brittle and breaks under heat cycling and chain oscillations. When the guides fail, the chain can slip or break, causing piston-to-valve contact and total engine destruction. Symptoms include a rattling noise on cold start and a "tractor-like" sound from the engine.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW Z4 sDrive20i (E89, 2011-2016) in fair condition is worth £6,000-£14,000 depending on mileage and specification. A preventative timing chain replacement at specialist rates (£1,200-£1,800) is excellent value on any Z4 sDrive20i. If the chain has snapped and the engine is destroyed, a £2,200-£3,600 rebuilt engine with warranty is a sound investment on a car worth over £8,000.
problems.recommendation: The N20 timing chain is the single biggest risk on the E89 Z4 sDrive20i. If you hear a rattling noise on cold start, do not drive the car - have it inspected immediately. Preventative chain replacement at a specialist costs significantly less than a full engine replacement. On any N20-powered Z4 approaching 70,000 miles without documented chain work, this is essential preventative maintenance.

problems.rootCause: The N46 timing chain tensioner can wear out, leading to a rattling noise from the engine. If not addressed, the timing chain can slip or break, causing severe engine damage. Oil leaks from the valve cover gasket and oil filter housing are also extremely common and can lead to low oil levels and further damage if ignored.

If the engine has suffered catastrophic damage, carefully evaluate whether a rebuilt engine is financially sensible - for a well-maintained example in good condition, the investment can be justified.
problems.recommendation: The N46 timing chain tensioner is a known weak point. If you hear a rattling noise on start-up, have it inspected immediately. Oil leaks should also be addressed promptly - low oil levels from leaks can accelerate timing chain wear. Regular oil changes with the correct specification oil are critical to N46 longevity.

problems.group: BMW Z4 20i N20 Fuel Injector & Ignition Coil Failure
problems.h4: BMW Z4 20i N20 Fuel Injector & Ignition Coil Failure - Misfires and Rough Running
problems.rootCause: The N20's direct injection system can suffer from fuel injector failure, causing misfires and rough running. Ignition coils are also known to fail. Fault codes typically point to specific cylinders (e.g., Cylinder 3 misfire).

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty injectors and ignition coils, clear adaptations
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early with misfire codes

repairOptions.longevity: Only required if injector failure caused bore wash or other damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For an E89 Z4 sDrive20i worth £6,000-£14,000, a £400-£800 injector and coil replacement is straightforward and cost-effective.
problems.recommendation: Misfire codes on the N20 should not be ignored. Injector and coil replacement is a well-understood repair on these engines. If you experience rough running or hesitation, have the car diagnosed promptly - catching it early prevents secondary damage.
